messages:
maya: Ran perfetto + nsys on the longseq workload (seq=4096, microbatch=2). Seeing a narrow ~120ms window where HBM bandwidth spikes and throughput collapses. Uploading traces now.
perf-bot: perfetto trace available: https://perfetto.app/trace/xyz-1834506789 (nvtx + gpu counters)
arjun: thanks. quick q: is the spike during decode only or also during kv read/write phases?
maya: primarily during decode step 2 -> kv_read_async starts, then multiple cuda kernels fire: kv_page_scan, kv_read_merge, gpt_attn_fwd. HBM bw peaks ~420 GB/s in the trace sample.
sam: can you paste the nsys timeline sample (top hot kernels)? a short list is fine.
maya: nsys top kernels (ordered by time):
```
1) kv_read_async (35% time, heavy DRAM reads)
2) kv_page_scan (18%)
3) gpt_attn_fwd (12%)
4) fused_qk_mul (7%)
5) cudaMemcpyAsync (HBM->device) (6%)
```
maya: also saw lots of tiny memcpy spikes at boundaries, looks like eviction/reload waves when seqlen > 3072.
iris: eviction waves = KV entries getting evicted then re-fetched? that smells like hash-bucket thrash under large seq.
arjun: yeah, likely the per-token KV lookup pattern for long sequences is defeating the cache line usage. two levers: increase microbatch to amortize lookups or change kernel to fused prefetch/gather.
sam: we tried a fused-kv-gather patch last quarter that reduced small memcpy apparent events. did maya test that branch?
maya: ran on mainline. I repeated trace with the kv-fused-prefetch branch — peak HBM dropped ~25% and latency tail improved, but still see intermittent 50-80ms stalls. attaching the two perfetto links for compare.
perf-bot: perfetto trace (kv-fused-prefetch) uploaded: https://perfetto.app/trace/xyz-1834506795
arjun: curious if the stall correlates with kernel selection. maybe scheduler picks a non-fused kernel for >1 microbatch or picks an attention kernel variant that materializes large tensors. any chance the kernel selector uses heuristics based on seq_len that need tuning?
maya: yes, kernel selection log shows we fallback to the tiled-attn path for seq>=2048 in some batches because combined token window triggers different tiling estimates.
iris: quick idea: add a sequence-length-aware batching heuristic that pins microbatch to 1 for seq>2048 to avoid mixing short+long that trigger bad tiling choices. also try hinting the selector to prefer fused-kv when KV read ratio > 0.4.
sam: +1. can we also change the eviction threshold temporarily (raise cache_capacity by 10%) to see if eviction frequency drops? that should be low-risk to test on staging.
maya: will run 3 experiments: (A) fused-kv-prefetch branch w/ current batching, (B) selector hint + prefer fused-kv, (C) increase cache cap + prefer fused-kv. I'll attach perfetto + nsys for each. ETA EOD PST.
arjun: for nsys, use: `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=longseq-experiment -w true` and include `--capture-range=nvtx` around the decode window. helps isolate the hot window.
maya: good call, using that. also enabling the HBM counters set: `--cuda-memory-usage --gpu-metrics-device=all` for the HBM numbers.
iris: one more: record the kernel selection decision dump (we have a debug flag: `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select`), that will help see why tiled path wins.
maya: noted. logging that in experiment runs.
sam: awesome. if (B) shows good improvement we should land a selector tweak + add a unit test for mixed-seq batch scenarios.
arjun: also file a perf regression ticket if any patch increases tail latency on small sequences. want post-merge guardrails.
maya: will post results + traces to this thread when done. tagging @arjun @sam @iris for visibility. :eyes:
